A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MagicQuill. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplements support comparison, with retained content identifiable across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-editing and intent-prediction experiments on 490 images, a 30-participant user study, and supplementary qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds editing-time measurements, MagicBrush benchmark results and further qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The three-module system, brush-to-condition processing, diffusion architecture and LLaVA fine-tuning objective remain unchanged. Section 6.1 clarifies the use of separate edge and color ControlNets without establishing a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds MagicBrush evaluation covering single-turn and multi-turn instruction-guided editing, substantially extending evaluation beyond the constructed DCI test set and original user study. It also adds explicit complex-prompt and large-brush-area scenarios. Existing training and evaluation datasets are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated stroke-based comparators SDEdit and Uni-Paint in Figure 7. The new MagicBrush comparison evaluates InstructP2P, OmniGEN, SeedX, DDIM+PNP, Ledits++ and InfEdit in Table 4 and Figure 12. The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include single-turn and multi-turn MagicBrush evaluation using L1, L2, CLIP-I, DINO and CLIP-T, plus a with/without-Assistor timing comparison on iPad and PC, described as 10 users performing 10 edits. The original 490-image evaluations and stated training settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds an analysis of the Assistor's contribution to editing time, an edge-extractor comparison, and cases testing complex prompts and large control areas. These substantially broaden the questions examined beyond the retained failure cases, base-model generalization and context-dependent intent examples.

E5.justification: The original usability comparison retains the same standard-deviation error bars, moving from Figure 8 to Figure 9. V2 adds no repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new timing study reports averages without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original user-study results are unchanged. New results include with/without-Assistor times of 13.29/17.70 seconds on iPad and 12.49/15.53 seconds on PC, MagicBrush scores and qualitative outputs. Table 4 reports MagicQuill leading on L1, L2, CLIP-I and DINO, while InfEdit leads on CLIP-T in both settings. Reported generation cost also changes from 2 seconds/15 GB to 3 seconds/10 GB, without establishing comparable measurement hardware.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same mathematical operations and objectives. The function-argument correction in Section 3.1 aligns the prose notation with the existing equation; it does not revise mathematical reasoning. Neither version contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about precise brush-based editing, automatic intent prediction and improved usability and efficiency. The added experiments supply evidence for these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 newly discusses possible conflicts between edge and color signals and their weighted combination. It also explains PiDiNet selection through a balance between geometric preservation and human-like strokes. The original limitations concerning sketch–prompt conflict, colorization detail loss and ambiguous intent remain.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies separate ControlNets with default weights of 0.5 each, explicitly identifies the processor's PiDiNet extractor, and reports five hours of Assistor training on three A6000 GPUs. It revises the 512×512 generation estimate from 2 seconds and 15 GB VRAM to 3 seconds and 10 GB. Most implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands citation coverage and explicitly lists stroke-based and reference-based editing, adding works such as SDEdit, Uni-Paint, AnyDoor and MangaNinja. Next-GPT is removed. These updates broaden the literature coverage while preserving the central research positioning and novelty argument.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains intact. V2 moves cross-platform implementation text from Section 3.3 into the supplement, expands the Section 4.2 heading, renumbers appendix sections, adds acknowledgments and makes small wording and notation corrections.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the displayed evidence through two new tables and five new figures covering timing, stroke-based comparisons, edge extraction, MagicBrush, complex prompts and large brush areas. Existing figures are retained and rearranged, including the questionnaire and user gallery; the original user-study charts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 3 directly supports the efficiency claim previously assessed through user ratings, while MagicBrush and the added comparisons broaden empirical support. Implementation clarifications also help reproducibility. However, the MagicBrush brush-input construction and evaluation procedure remain sparsely documented, and the timing study lacks uncertainty estimates. The additions therefore support a limited overall improvement.
